name: The field and the knower of the field (kṣetra–kṣetrajña)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13: the body is the field and the one who knows it the knower of the field (13.2); Kṛṣṇa is the knower in all fields and the knowledge of both is knowledge (13.3); the field comprises the great elements, ahaṅkāra, buddhi, the unmanifest, the senses and their ranges, desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience and steadiness with their modifications (13.6–7); every being is born from their union (13.27); the possessor of the field illumines it as the sun the world (13.34); those who know their difference with the eye of knowledge go to the supreme (13.35).

name: The virtues called knowledge (BhG 13.7–11)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13.8–12 (vulgate 13.7–11): twenty dispositions are declared 'knowledge' (jñāna), and what is other than them 'ignorance'. The verse lists them without further grouping.

members: seeing again and again the evil of birth, death, old age, sickness and pain
anabhiṣvaṅga toward son, wife, home and the like (absence of clinging)
constant samacittatva in wanted and unwanted events (evenness of citta)
unswerving bhakti to Kṛṣṇa by ananya-yoga
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva (constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self)
tattvajñānārtha-darśana (keeping in view the aim of knowledge of reality)
notes: The count of twenty depends on counting asakti and anabhiṣvaṅga separately and the two items of 13.12 separately; the text itself gives no number. This edition numbers the verses 13.8–12.

name: The three guṇas

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 14: sattva, rajas and tamas arise from prakṛti and bind the imperishable embodied one in the body (14.5). Sattva, stainless, illuminating and free of affliction, binds by attachment to happiness and knowledge; rajas, of the nature of passion, by attachment to action; tamas, born of ignorance and deluding, by heedlessness, idleness and sleep (14.6–9). Each prevails by overpowering the other two (14.10). Signs: illumination-knowledge at all the body's gates (sattva); greed, activity, undertaking, restlessness, craving (rajas); absence of illumination, inactivity, heedlessness, delusion (tamas) (14.11–13). Dying in each leads respectively to the stainless worlds of the knowers, birth among those attached to action, and deluded wombs (14.14–15); their fruits are the stainless, pain and ignorance (14.16); from them come knowledge, greed, and heedlessness, delusion and ignorance (14.17); their followers go upward, stay in the middle, go downward (14.18). One who sees no agent but the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains Kṛṣṇa's state (14.19); going beyond them one attains the immortal (14.20; marks 14.22–25; means 14.26).

name: Perishable, imperishable and the Supreme Person

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.16–19: there are two persons (puruṣa) in the world, the perishable — all beings — and the imperishable, the one standing firm (kūṭastha); the highest person is another, called the supreme self, the imperishable lord who enters and sustains the three worlds; because Kṛṣṇa is beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable he is renowned in world and Veda as puruṣottama; one who knows him so knows all and worships him with his whole being.

notes: What the akṣara denotes is read differently by the commentators (see the teaching notes on 15.16).

name: The inverted aśvattha tree of saṃsāra

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.1–5: 'they speak of' an imperishable aśvattha with roots above and branches below, its leaves the metres; knowing it one knows the Veda; its branches spread below and above, swollen by the guṇas, with sense-objects as shoots, and its roots below are bound up with action in the human world; its form, end, beginning and foundation are not perceived here; having cut it with the strong weapon of non-attachment one is to seek the place of no return, taking refuge in the primal person from whom the ancient activity flowed; the undeluded, free of pride, delusion, attachment and desire, reach that imperishable place. (The verses do not themselves name the tree saṃsāra.)

name: The self is not the agent; the guṇas act

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–14: prakṛti is the cause in agency (13.21); one who sees actions done by prakṛti alone and his self as not the doer sees (13.30); the supreme self, beginningless and without guṇas, though in the body neither acts nor is tainted (13.32), as space is not tainted (13.33); the seer who beholds no agent other than the guṇas attains Kṛṣṇa's state (14.19).

name: The guṇas as the doers of action

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 14.19: the seer beholds no agent other than the guṇas; 14.23: the one gone beyond the guṇas stays firm, (knowing) only that 'the guṇas are operating'.

name: The conjunction of puruṣa and prakṛti (saṃyoga)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13: puruṣa, situated in prakṛti, experiences the guṇas born of prakṛti, and attachment to them causes its births in good and bad wombs (13.22); whatever being is born, moving or unmoving, is from the union (saṃyoga) of the field and the knower of the field (13.27).

name: Prakṛti (primordial nature)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–14: beginningless like puruṣa; the modifications and guṇas arise from it (13.20); the cause in agency (13.21); actions are done by it alone (13.30); the three guṇas are born of it (14.5).

name: Puruṣa (the conscious self)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13: beginningless like prakṛti (13.20); the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain (13.21); situated in prakṛti it experiences the guṇas, and attachment to them causes its births (13.22); 'the highest puruṣa in this body' is named onlooker, consenter, supporter, experiencer, great lord and supreme self (13.23). Chapter 15 speaks of two puruṣas in the world and a highest puruṣa (15.16–18).

name: Brahman (the ultimate ground)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–14: the knowable is the beginningless supreme brahman, neither sat nor asat (13.13); it has hands, feet, eyes and ears everywhere and stands enveloping all (13.14); appears through the sense-qualities yet is without senses, is unattached yet supports all, without guṇas yet their experiencer (13.15); is inside and outside beings, moving and unmoving, not to be known through subtlety, far and near (13.16); undivided yet as if divided, sustainer, devourer and generator of beings (13.17); light of lights beyond darkness, knowledge, knowable and reached by knowledge, set in the heart of all (13.18); seeing the many as resting in the one one attains brahman (13.31); by unswerving devotion one becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26); Kṛṣṇa is the foundation of brahman (14.27).

name: The Lord in the heart of all beings

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.15: Kṛṣṇa says he is seated in the heart of all, and that memory, knowledge and their loss come from him. (13.18 says the knowable brahman is set in the heart of all.)

name: The soul as a part (aṃśa) of Brahman

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.7: 'a portion (aṃśa) of me alone, eternal, having become the living being in the world of the living' draws the senses with the mind — the text says 'of me' (Kṛṣṇa), not 'of brahman'.

notes: The commentators divide on whether the portion is apparent, a real part as mode, or a separated part.

name: The self common to all men (vaiśvānara)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.14: Kṛṣṇa, becoming Vaiśvānara and dwelling in the bodies of breathing beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, digests the fourfold food.

name: The paths of the Gītā: action, knowledge, meditation and devotion

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13.25–26: some see the self in themselves by meditation, others by sāṃkhya-yoga, others by karma-yoga; others, not knowing thus, worship on hearing from others, and they too cross death. (This passage names meditation, sāṃkhya, action and worship-by-hearing, not a fourfold scheme.)

name: Rebirth

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: attachment to the guṇas causes puruṣa's births in good and bad wombs (13.22); one who knows puruṣa and prakṛti is not born again (13.24); dying in sattva, rajas or tamas leads to the stainless worlds, to birth among those attached to action, or to deluded wombs (14.14–15, 14.18); the living being takes the senses and mind with it from body to body as the wind carries scents (15.8).

name: The great brahman as womb and the Lord as seed-giving father (BhG 14.3–4)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 14.3–4: Kṛṣṇa calls the great brahman (mahad brahma) his womb, in which he places the embryo; from it is the origin of all beings; of whatever forms arise in all wombs, the great brahman is the womb and he the seed-giving father.

notes: The commentators identify the great brahman here with prakṛti; the text does not use that word.

name: Dying while a guṇa predominates (BhG 14.14–15, 14.18)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 14.14–15, 14.18: if the embodied one dies when sattva has increased, he reaches the stainless worlds of those who know the highest; dying in rajas he is born among those attached to action; dying in tamas, in the wombs of the deluded; those in sattva go upward, the rājasa stay in the middle, the tāmasa go downward.

name: Devotion (bhakti)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: unswerving devotion to Kṛṣṇa by a yoga with no other is counted among the dispositions called knowledge (13.11); his devotee, knowing field, knowledge and knowable, becomes fit for his state (13.19); one who serves him with the unswerving yoga of devotion goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26); one who knows him as puruṣottama worships him with his whole being (15.19).

name: The eternal, unslayable embodied one (dehin / śarīrin)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 14.5: the guṇas bind the imperishable embodied one (dehinam avyayam) in the body; 14.20: the embodied one who goes beyond them attains the immortal.

name: Equanimity (samatva)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–14: constant evenness of citta in wanted and unwanted events is among the dispositions called knowledge (13.10); the one gone beyond the guṇas is alike in pain and pleasure, clod, stone and gold, pleasant and unpleasant, blame and praise, honour and dishonour, friend and foe (14.24–25); one who sees the lord the same in all beings sees (13.28–29).

name: Teacher, transmission and secrecy in the Gītā and epic

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: the teaching on field and knower has been sung by the seers, in the metres and in the brahmasūtra words (13.5); attendance on the teacher is among the dispositions called knowledge (13.8); some worship having heard from others (13.26); the knowledge of the guṇas is announced as the highest, by which all the sages reached perfection (14.1); chapter 15 is called 'this most secret teaching' (15.20).

name: The self as witness

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13.23: the highest puruṣa in this body is called the onlooker (upadraṣṭṛ), with consenter, supporter, experiencer, great lord and supreme self. (The Gītā's word here is upadraṣṭṛ, not sākṣin.)

name: Surrender to the Lord (śaraṇāgati / prapatti)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 15.4: after cutting the aśvattha, the place of no return is to be sought with the words 'I take refuge (prapadye) in that very primal person from whom the ancient activity flowed forth'.

name: The twenty-four principles (epic Sāṃkhya)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13.6–7: the field is listed as the great elements, ahaṅkāra, buddhi, the unmanifest, the ten senses and the one, the five ranges of the senses, with desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience and steadiness; the text does not number them.
